appendix_title: ŚAIVĀGAMA DIVISIONS IN FIVE STREAMS (according to the five faces of Śiva)
content:
Appendix I
ŚAIVĀGAMA DIVISIONS
IN FIVE STREAMS
(according to the five faces of Śiva)

तथा हि सर्गादौ परमेश्वरः ऊर्ध्वप्राग्दक्षिणोत्तर पश्चिमस्त्रोतः
पंचकभेदभिन्नं ज्ञानम् (Mṛgendra-tantra-vṛtti, Intro.)

The entries in each of the five divisions are: (i)
Karaņeśvara, (ii) the sage initiated, (iii) the gocara-
progenitors and their origin and number, (iv) the Āgama-
class; (v) the texts; (vi) the type of Śāstra; and (vii) the
mantra specific to the division.

I TATPURUŚĀ (East):
(Rudra-division)
(i) Isvara; (ii) Gautama; (iii) Sāvitrī-gocaras, born out
of nāda and 30 in number; (iv) Gāruḍa; (v) Trotala etc.;
(vi) Ati-mārga; (vii) Bahu-rūpa

II AGHORA (South):
(Rudra-division)
(i) Rudra; (ii) Bhāradvāja; (iii) Jyotir-gocaras, born
out of bindu, and 20 in number; (iv) Bhairava; (v) Asita
etc.;
(vi) Adhyātma; (vii) Aghora.

III SADYOJĀTA (West):
(Śiva-division)
(i) Brahmā; (ii) Kāśyapa; (iii) Śiva-gocaras, born out
of Śiva, and 25 in number; (vi) Bhūta; (v) Caṇḍasidhāra
etc.; (vi) Laukika; (vii) Guhya.

IV VĀMADEVA (North) (Śiva-division)
(i) Viṣṇu; (ii) Kauśika; (iii) Śikhā-gocaras, born out
of Śakti; and 25 in number; (iv) Vāma; (v) Sammoha etc.;
(vi) Vaidika; (vii) Vārna.

V ĪŚĀNA (Upper, Ūrdhva) (Rudra-division)
(i) Sadāśiva; (ii) Agastya or Atri; (iii) Vyoma-gocaras,
origin not mentioned, 20 in number; (iv) Siddhanta; (v)
Kāmika etc.; (vi) Mantra-tantra; (vii) Īsa.

इदं ज्ञानं सिद्धान्तं परमं शुभम्।
ऊर्ध्वस्त्रोतोद्भवं अष्टाविशंतिकतन्त्रकम्।।
(Makuṭāgama, 1,22-3)
cf. Pūrva-kāraņa. 26.44-49;
Suprabhada. caryā 1,22-28.
summary: This appendix details the classification of Śaivāgama traditions into five streams, each corresponding to one of the five faces of Śiva. The five streams are Tatpuruṣa (East), Aghora (South), Sadyojāta (West), Vāmadeva (North), and Īśāna (Upper). For each stream, it lists seven defining characteristics: the Karaṇeśvara (presiding deity), the initiated sage, the gocara-progenitors, the Āgama class, specific texts, the type of Śāstra, and the specific mantra. The streams are further grouped into 'Rudra-division' and 'Śiva-division'. The information is based on the Mṛgendra-tantra-vṛtti and is supported by quotes from other texts like the Makuṭāgama.
purpose: The purpose of this appendix is to provide a systematic and structured framework for understanding the vast and complex body of Śaivāgama literature and tradition. It organizes the different schools of thought, texts, and practices into five distinct streams based on the theological concept of Śiva's five faces, making the interrelationships within the tradition clearer.
key_information: The Śaivāgamas are divided into five streams (srotas) based on the five faces of Śiva.
The five streams and their associated faces/directions are: TATPURUŚĀ (East), AGHORA (South), SADYOJĀTA (West), VĀMADEVA (North), and ĪŚĀNA (Upper, Ūrdhva).

Each stream is defined by seven attributes: (i) Karaņeśvara, (ii) the sage initiated, (iii) the gocara-progenitors, (iv) the Āgama-class, (v) the texts, (vi) the type of Śāstra, and (vii) the specific mantra.
The streams are further categorized into a 'Rudra-division' (Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Īśāna) and a 'Śiva-division' (Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva).
The primary source cited for this classification is the Mṛgendra-tantra-vṛtti.
The appendix concludes with a Sanskrit quote from the Makuṭāgama and references to the Pūrva-kāraṇa and Suprabheda āgamas, likely to corroborate the information on the Īśāna stream.
